The following is an excerpt from the diary of Lena Muchina translated into English. Lena survived the German attack/besiegement on Leningrad during the Second World War. During the Nazi encirclement and bombardment of Leningrad, thousands of civilians were blocked from escape without food. An estimated 700,000 civilians died of starvation.

January 2nd, 1942

It's already been so long since I've put my pen to the paper. Let's see, what hasn't happened since I last wrote.

The new year of 1942 has begun.

Mama and I are alone now. Aka has died. She died on her birthday, the same day she turned 76. It happened yesterday, on the first of January at nine in the morning. I wasn't at home when it happened. I was out getting our bread rations. I was wondering to myself why Aka had been lying so still and quiet as I was coming back from the bakery. Mama was very calm on the outside, as she always is, and told me that Aka was just sleeping. We drank some tea, and Mama had cut me a small piece of Aka's bread. She said, that Aka won't be eating too much of it anyways. After that Mama suggested that I go with her to the theater to get lunch. (Lena's Mama is actually her aunt, as her biological mother died last year. "Mama" works at a theater and is able to get more food through her job than regular non-workers are otherwise allowed.) I agreed, and said that I was afraid to stay at home with Aka alone. If she were to suddenly die, what should I do? I was afraid, that Mama would ask me to take care of Aka while she was gone. I didn't want to go into Aka's room, and be filled with dread having to see how she died. I was accustomed to give Aka anything, the lovely, good, busy old woman who always had something to do. And suddenly Aka is bed-stricken, laying helplessly there, skin and bones, with barely enough energy to hold anything in her hands.

So I didn't really want to see Aka, and that's why I was happy to go with Mama to the theater. Mama then closed and locked the door. (They live in a community shared apartment, such that many families all live in the same building with separate rooms, rather than individual "apartments".)

"Mama, why did you lock Aka inside? What if she needs something?"

But Mama answered me, that Aka doesn't need anything anymore, That Aka has died.

"When?"

"When you went to get bread. I sent you out on purpose."

"Why? I wouldn't have decided on my own to stay alone in a room with a dead person. Did she say goodbye to you?"

"No, she didn't say anything."

And so it was, that Aka didn't exist anymore, that Aka is no longer there.

....

Mama and I are now alone. I have no one except for Mama Lena, and she has no one except for me. Now I have to protect Mama like I've never done before. If she dies, then I am lost. Where should I go if I'm left alone? What would I do? Mama is now only living through her bravery. Her bravery is strong. She knows that she can't give up, because I'm by her side now.
